title: Usage laddering and pro-rata burst pricing PRD and acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a new pricing construct called 'usage laddering' which combines tiered per-unit pricing with short-term burst allowances and pro-rata adjustments for mid-cycle plan changes. The goal is to: reduce invoice surprises for customers, allow predictable sustained discounts, and provide controlled burst capacity without complex manual credits.

Scope:
- Metering: extend existing usage key to include 'ladder_band' dimension (values: sustained, burst, overage) and persist effective unit price per event.
- Billing: calculate pro-rated charge/credit when a customer upgrades or downgrades mid-cycle; generate separate invoice line items for laddering adjustments.
- Quotas/Rate limits: allow configurable burst windows per plan (e.g., 1m, 5m) enforced via token-bucket in proxy; ensure throttles and billing are decoupled so throttled requests are free of charge.
- Console: surface an "effective per-unit" metric on the usage page, show ladder band breakdown and a simulated invoice preview when a customer changes plans.
- Backfill/retroactive changes: define reconciliation for plan changes older than 14 days (automatic refund or manual review).

Out-of-scope for initial rollout:
- Cross-tenant credit pooling.
- Complex entitlement slices that dynamically redistribute credits across products.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Server-side enforcement of burst windows keeps client simple but increases proxy load; chosen to ensure consistent billing and prevent gaming.
- Persisting per-event effective unit price increases storage and ingestion costs but enables exact invoice reconstruction and customer dispute resolution.
- Pro-rating on upgrade is automatic; on downgrade we prefer issuing credit on next invoice rather than immediate refund to simplify payment flows.

Data model changes (high level):
- Metering event fields: tenant_id, route_id, model_id, tokens, timestamp, ladder_band, effective_unit_price_cents, invoice_period_id.
- Invoice line items: type (consumption|ladder_adjustment), description, quantity, unit_price_cents, period_start, period_end, reference_event_range.

Billing pipeline integration notes:
- Ingest laddered events into Billing-ETL stage; add aggregator that groups by invoice_period_id and ladder_band to compute subtotal lines.
- Add reconciliation job (daily) that detects mid-cycle plan changes and emits adjustment line items with tags for manual review when delta > $5k.

Console UX changes:
- Usage modal: new toggles to show breakdown by ladder band (sustained|burst|overage).
- Plan change flow: invoice preview modal showing pro-rated delta and next-invoice projection.

Acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria field for atomic items):
1) Metering: events contain ladder_band and effective_unit_price_cents for 100% of consumption after rollout.
2) Billing: mid-cycle upgrade generates a pro-rated invoice line that matches simulated preview to within $0.50 for sample accounts.
3) Rate limit enforcement: burst windows are enforced without billing requests that were throttled.
4) Console: customers can view ladder band breakdown and see an invoice preview when changing plans.
5) Reconciliation: the daily job emits adjustment items for plan changes with delta > $0 and flags deltas > $5k for manual ops review.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests: billing math, pro-rate formulas, meter ingestion mapping.
- End-to-end: 3 sandbox tenants with synthetic traffic patterns (sustained, bursty, blended); verify invoices and console UI.
- Canary: enable feature for 1% of tenants with automated checks on invoice delta variance and ingestion error rates for 48 hours before ramping.

- Design spec (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/usage-laddering-design-2026
- Billing ETL PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1342
- Proxy enforcement PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/897
- Dashboard (canary metrics): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/usage-laddering-canary

Open questions for engineering:
- Does storing effective_unit_price_cents at event level require schema migration windows? (Action: infra/engineering to propose migration plan by 2026-02-22)
- Threshold for manual review is tentative at $5k — if finance prefers $2k we need to adjust the flag.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Billing: Sanjay Mehta (owner)

Rollout checklist:
- [ ] Billing ETL PR merged and smoke-tested
- [ ] Proxy token-bucket rollout behind feature flag
- [ ] Console UI toggles implemented and feature-flagged
- [ ] Canary metrics pass for 48 hours
- [ ] Finance sign-off on invoice preview language
- [ ] Release billing-2026.04
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: Metering events must include ladder_band and effective_unit_price_cents for 100% of consumption after feature flag is enabled for a tenant.
AC-002: Pro-rated upgrade invoice line is generated at the moment of plan change and matches the console preview within $0.50 for sample test accounts.
AC-003: Burst windows enforced by proxy do not result in charged tokens for throttled requests; billing records show zero cost for throttled events.
AC-004: Console displays ladder band breakdown and an invoice preview when a tenant initiates a plan change; preview calculation uses same billing logic as pipeline.
AC-005: Daily reconciliation job emits adjustment items for mid-cycle plan changes; items with delta > $5k are flagged and routed to finance/ops inbox.
AC-006: End-to-end tests for three synthetic tenant profiles pass in staging: sustained, bursty, blended (invoice variance < 1% vs expected).
